hypotheses.cause: Existing ST% is price-status-sensitive because its EOH/inventory inputs are computed after the base aggregation already filters by the user's prodlife/price-status scope, not because of an error in the sell_thru_pct formula itself

root_cause.statement: sell_thru_pct's denominator terms (last_value_eoh_u, last_value_eoh_intransit_u) are sourced from _BASE_SUM_SALES_METRICS_/_BASE_SUM_RCPT_METRICS_ tables that already apply `WHERE prodlife IN (${LEAF_PRODLIFE})` (history_metrics_ty.ftl:129,251,371) — LEAF_PRODLIFE is driven by the user's price-status/merchcat filter selection. So when a planner filters to FP-only, last_value_eoh_u reflects FP-only EOH, not total EOH — making ST% price-status-sensitive contrary to the business intent stated in the ticket and matching SUP-4488's AEO bug exactly.

knowledge_gained.technical: Across S5 pivots, 'price-status agnostic' inventory metrics (Total Available Inv U) can silently inherit a price-status scope when they're computed downstream of a base aggregation table that already WHERE-filters by prodlife/merchcat (see history_metrics_ty.ftl BASE_SUM_* tables). Any metric meant to be status-agnostic needs its own unfiltered aggregation path, not just a formula tweak in COMPUTED_METRICS_PRUNED.
knowledge_gained.functional: Retail planners expect Sell-Through % to measure demand against the FULL available inventory position (regardless of whether that stock is currently priced Full Price or Markdown) — filtering the view to 'FP only' should narrow which SALES count in the numerator, not shrink the inventory denominator. The current behavior conflates 'what I'm looking at' with 'what's actually on hand,' understating true sell-through whenever a price-status filter is applied.
